jobs.occupation: Midwife with International Experience Wanted for the Labour Ward at Aalborg University Hospital
jobs.description:
Become Part of a Unique Community – Midwife with International Experience Wanted for the Labour Ward at Aalborg University Hospital
Do you dream of working in a place where professional excellence, compassion, and development go hand in hand? 
Where you are surrounded every day by dedicated colleagues, and where your skills and experience are recognised, utilised, and appreciated?
If so, this is your opportunity to join our fantastic maternity team at Aalborg University Hospital.

We are seeking a midwife with international experience and knowledge of different childbirth cultures for a permanent position, starting on 1 September 2026 or as soon as possible. We wish to expand our work on childbirth culture and cultural understanding and are therefore looking for a midwife who can contribute to this development. The position is not a development role, but a standard clinical midwife position on the labour ward with a special professional profile.

We expect you to have experience working as a midwife in a non-European country and to be fluent in a widely spoken world language other than English. You must have completed the Danish adaptation and evaluation employment programme and hold Danish authorisation as a midwife.

Why Choose Us?
At Aalborg University Hospital, you will find more than just a job—you will become part of a strong, supportive, and professionally inspiring community.
We are the largest maternity unit in the North Denmark Region. As a highly specialised department, we provide care for approximately 3,300 pregnant women, women in labour, postpartum women, and their families each year. Here, you will have the opportunity to apply your professional expertise in a dynamic environment with varied responsibilities and room for both specialisation and professional development.

In addition, we offer:

• A clinical supervising midwife on every shift as a dedicated professional mentor
• A personal coordinator during your onboarding period
• A buddy system on every shift
• Opportunities for professional courses, supervision, and targeted competency development
• Teams and professional communities that hold regular group meetings with both professional and social content
You will become part of a large and engaged professional community consisting of approximately 150 skilled colleagues—midwives, nurses, healthcare assistants, doctors, and administrative staff—all dedicated to creating safe, coordinated, and professional maternity care pathways.

Opportunities with Us
We understand that a long working life includes changing needs and interests. Therefore, we place great emphasis on flexibility and the opportunity to combine different functions according to your preferences.
This means you may combine work in areas such as:

• Labour Ward and Midwifery Antenatal Clinic
• Labour Ward and Maternity Assessment Unit
• Labour Ward and Postnatal Ward
The majority of our midwives work in combined positions like these, creating professional variety, development opportunities, and job satisfaction.
We highly prioritise education and professional growth, and as a midwife with us, you will be part of a workplace where learning and development are natural parts of everyday practice.

Who Are You?
You are a qualified midwife with substantial professional experience from another country and exposure to a different childbirth culture.
You thrive in a professionally strong environment where teamwork, safety, and professionalism are central values.
You are passionate about working in the birthing suite. You enjoy building new relationships and work confidently both in complex obstetric cases and in births where the most important task is simply “being there” for the woman and her family.
You are able to identify the differences between childbirth cultures and contribute valuable insights and reflections to the daily professional discussions on the labour ward.

In addition, we expect that you are fluent in a widely spoken world language other than English. You must have completed the Danish adaptation and evaluation employment programme and hold Danish authorisation as a midwife.

Most importantly, you:

• Want to become part of a committed and caring team
• Contribute positively to a supportive and developmental work environment
• Are passionate about creating safe and coherent childbirth experiences
Our Values – Your Foundation
Our work is based on the North Denmark Region’s core values: Involvement, Trust, Decency, and Professionalism (I-TOP).
This means that we meet women, families, and relatives with empathy and respect—and we treat each other in the same way.

We Offer You

• A workplace characterised by high professional standards, warmth, and humour
• Strong interdisciplinary collaboration where everyone contributes
• A quality standard that ensures one midwife for every woman in labour
• A work environment where psychological and physical well-being are prioritised
• Supervision by trained supervisors in structured group programmes
• A unique collaboration between Health and Safety Representatives, Union Representatives, and Management, based on openness, respect, and trust
• A department where ideas are encouraged and where your voice matters
• A workplace that values your experience and is genuinely curious about your professional background
And last—but certainly not least:
The best colleagues in the world and a workplace you look forward to coming to every day.

Salary and Employment Conditions
Salary and employment terms according to the current collective agreement for non-managing midwives, etc., concluded with the Danish Midwives' Association.

Further Information
For questions about the position, please contact:
Arianne Brandborg Nørhave
Acting Deputy Head Midwife and Manager of the Labour Ward
Phone: +45 20 73 07 50
Email: a.noerhave@rn.dk

Recruitment Process
Application deadline: 20th of september 2026
Please submit your application, CV, and any other relevant documents electronically to this e-mail: m.cederstroem@rn.dk

Interviews: Expected to take place shortly after the application deadline.

Starting date: 1th of October 2026 or earlier by agreement.

jobs.occupation: Paving Worker / Landscaping Construction Worker – Practical Skills
jobs.description:
Work location: Denmark
Working hours: 37 hours per week
Employment type: Full-time, permanent position
Salary: After qualificatons
Start date: By agreement

About the position

We are looking for practical and reliable employees to carry out paving and landscaping construction work in Denmark.

The position is suitable for candidates who have good practical skills, an aptitude for manual work and an interest in construction and outdoor work.

A formal vocational qualification as a paving worker or landscaper is not required.

Instead, we value practical experience, a good understanding of manual work, accuracy, reliability and the ability to learn new working methods.

Main duties

The work will primarily include:

• 
Paving and surfacing work

• 
Laying paving stones, concrete slabs, cobblestones, kerbstones and other paving materials

• 
Measuring, setting out and preparing work areas

• 
Excavation and preparation of ground and sub-base

• 
Levelling and compacting sub-base and sand

• 
Cutting and adapting paving materials

• 
Establishing and adjusting edges, levels and gradients

• 
Minor landscaping and groundworks

• 
Using hand tools and small construction machinery

• 
General maintenance and cleaning of the work area

• 
Following applicable health, safety and environmental regulations

The exact tasks may vary depending on the project and the employee's practical experience.

We are looking for someone who

• 
Has a natural aptitude for practical and manual work

• 
Is comfortable with physically demanding work

• 
Works accurately and takes pride in the quality of their work

• 
Can work independently based on instructions

• 
Works well as part of a team

• 
Is reliable, punctual and responsible

• 
Is motivated to learn and develop practical skills

• 
Preferably has previous experience in paving, landscaping, construction, groundworks, installation, renovation or other practical work

A formal vocational qualification is not required.

Relevant practical experience from construction, civil works, groundworks, installation, renovation, agriculture or other practical occupations is considered an advantage.

Language requirements

English is an advantage.

Danish is not required at the time of employment. However, the employee must be able to understand relevant work instructions and health and safety instructions sufficiently to perform the work safely.

Salary and employment conditions

The fixed and guaranteed salary is:

DKK 37,500 gross per month for 37 hours of work per week.

In addition, the employer provides an occupational pension in accordance with the applicable employment terms.

The fixed cash salary corresponds to your qualifications

The salary is fixed and guaranteed and is not dependent on bonuses, commissions or overtime.

Employment conditions, including working hours, pension, holiday entitlement, overtime and notice periods, will be specified in the employment contract and will comply with applicable Danish legislation and customary Danish employment conditions for the position.

Occupation / DISCO-08

DISCO-08: 711220 – Paving Work

The position specifically involves paving and surfacing work, including the preparation, installation and finishing of paved surfaces.

What we offer

• 
Permanent full-time employment in Denmark

• 
37-hour working week

• 
Fixed salary matched to your qualifications

• 
Training and introduction to the company's working methods

• 
Varied projects within paving and landscaping construction

• 
A professional working environment

• 
Opportunity to develop practical and manual skills

How to apply

Please send your CV and a short description of your previous work experience.

You do not need to have a formal vocational qualification.

Instead, please describe the practical work you have previously performed, the tools or machinery you have experience using, and the types of tasks you are accustomed to carrying out.

Candidates will be assessed based on their practical experience, aptitude for manual work, motivation, reliability and ability to learn.

This is a genuine full-time position in Denmark and the vacancy will be advertised through Jobnet and EURES.

jobs.occupation: Chef- Zoku Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Are you a passionate chef with great cooking skills who loves to work in an open kitchen? Then keep reading.

Zoku provides a home for business travellers who want to live in a city for between a few days and a few months. We’re a new type of hotel offering a relaxed place to live, co-work and socialize – while wiring residents into the local scene. Join an international team of driven, proactive and fun-loving Zokus who all have one thing in common: a passion for connecting people across the globe.

TELL ME MORE

Life doesn’t become more social than through sharing food. That’s our founding food philosophy and it can be yours too. The food that comes out of our Living Kitchen is fresh, simple, honest, healthy and local. With short-end preparation times, simple ingredients and limited preparation steps, our assortment is incredibly intelligent and facilitates fast service.

As our new chef you'll be responsible for any food that comes out of our Living Kitchen. You'll plate beautiful dishes and at times make creative buffets that not only look good, but also taste amazing. 

You’ll work closely together with our team of chefs, to develop menu offerings and forecast supply needs. You like to take on responsibility, thrive with independence in your work and function as a substitute for our chefs. 

WHAT MAKES OUR KITCHEN UNIQUE?

• 
You won’t hide in the background. You'll get to work in an open kitchen environment with plenty of space and natural daylight.

• 
You'll get the ultimate flexibility. You can come up with your own dishes and let your creativity run wild.

• 
You can have good conversations with visitors. You’re the face of the kitchen and you'll get to directly chat with guests.

• 
You get to be independent in your work. You like doing your own thing and can cook solo when you need to.

• 
You can get to know the entire team. You'll be in close contact with our front of house and the entire Zoku team.

• 
You can work in a unique kitchen setup. We’re not like your average kitchen (feel free to stop by our rooftop to see for yourself!).

• 
You are encouraged to work with fresh and seasonal ingredients. We put a strong emphasis on incorporating vegetables into our dishes.

WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU?

• 
A market conform salary package including pension and health insurance.

• 
Cool benefits like an after-work drink, access to all community events, various discounts like 40% discount on F&B for you and 4 friends, plus Employee and Friends & Family rates in all Zoku Locations.  

• 
A free night stay for you and your +1 in your first 3 months at your Zoku (dinner & breakfast) and a free night at any Zoku location for your birthday, including welcome drink & breakfast to experience Zoku as a true guest. 

• 
No boring canteen!! Staff meals enjoyed from our Living Kitchen.

• 
A personal budget unlocked after 1 year at Zoku to spend on extra days off, learning & development, extra cash or discounted vouchers. 

• 
A fun, young, and international team to grow with. Plus, exciting training and events to celebrate every step of the journey!

• 
A job at one of the 25 coolest hotels in the world, that feels like a second home and is purpose-driven.

WE LOVE PEOPLE WHO...

• 
Show their creativity through their passion for food and never settle for less.

• 
Can juggle many tasks at the same time while remaining cool headed and warm hearted.

• 
Enjoy variety in their day and are happy to switch things up, whether that means breakfast, brunch, lunch buffets, a la carte dinners or cheffing up something special for our Meetings & Events.

• 
Have experience in working independently and don't believe in traditional kitchen hierarchies.

• 
Enjoy working in an open kitchen and love to chat up a storm with our residents.

• 
Have experience in healthy homestyle cooking – vegetarian cooking skills are a plus.

• 
Have provable knowledge of various cooking techniques.

A FEW MUST HAVES

• 
You have a minimum of 1 year working experience in a kitchen or restaurant environment. 

• 
You have experience with implementing the local HACCP guidelines (Hygiejnebevis).

• 
You are fluent in English – Danish and other languages are a plus.

• 
You are an EU resident or have a working and living permit valid for Denmark including a CPR.

• 
You are fully flexible, as there won't be fixed working days / hours, including availability on some weekends. Shifts include AM, Mid-shifts, and PM. 

• 
You love to work as we'll need you Full Time (37 hours- 5 shifts weekly)

• 
Available to start As Soon As Possible.

WHAT WE ARE PROUD OF 

Our fresh take on hospitality has been recognized around the world with plenty of press attention and design awards.

We’re also proudly B Corp certified at all four of our locations (Amsterdam, Copenhagen, Paris and Vienna), which means we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to social and environmental impact, transparency and accountability.

WHAT IS ZOKU

Zoku is a new type of hotel that offers a place to live, co-work and socialize in Europe's most livable cities: Amsterdam, Vienna, Copenhagen & Paris. 

Designed for the new generation of travellers, Zoku is so much more than a long stay hotel. It is a place you can call your second home, even on your first visit. Zoku is a hive of private Lofts and rooftop Social Spaces, so travellers can stay connected and well rested as they live and work throughout Europe. Throw yourself into your work and play, and effortlessly discover one of our home cities.

jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Engineering within Robotics
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Robotics. The candidate is expected to start on January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST) 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. 

 

Who are we looking for

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of Robotics, who is eager to develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

• 
Strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Have research experience in computer vision fields related to laboratory automation. This could include (but is not limited to) methods for:

• 
vision-based handling of laboratory equipment, in particular glassware and fluids 

• 
segmentation and vision-based handling of medical specimens and fluids

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of Robotics, such as robotics control, modelling, computer vision, medical/industrial robotics and artificial intelligence. 

• 
Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

• 
Be fluent in English.

• 
Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network, are considered comparative advantages.

• 
Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally. 

 

The Department

MMMI

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The institute is the origin of robotics research in Denmark and has spawned the world-renowned cluster of robotics in Odense with more than 130 robotics companies including Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots. Building on our expertise in AI, robotics and software, we have raised strong research centres in related domains, such as Health Informatics and Energy Informatics, Drones and other relevant research areas. 

SDU Robotics

SDU Robotics conducts research among others within the fields of robotics and computer vision. The unit focuses on research problems from real robotics applications within manufacturing industries, hospitals, elderly care, and other partners in society. The unit also focuses on Robot related vision technologies for facilitating industrial part feeding, automated product assembly, uncertainty aware quality inspection, and biomedical segmentation for diagnosis and robot control. 

SDU Robotics’ research involves mathematical modeling and control of robots, robotic processes and robot systems, human-robot interactions, computer vision for reliable inspection and robot control, and simulation technologies for robotics and computer vision aimed at closing the Sim2Real gap. Artificial Intelligence is widely applied within all research fields. 

 

Additional information

For further information about being a professor at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For more questions about the position please contact Head of Unit, Professor Thiusius Rajeeth Savarimuthu at trs@mmmi.sdu.dk.

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The candidate will be attached to The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute in Odense and is also expected to participate in DIAS activities and interdisciplinary cooperation in Odense regularly.
The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Further information on salary and taxation.

 

The tenure track programme the Faculty of Engineering is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area. Candidates enter the assistant professor level (for up to 6 years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position of associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee. Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented independent scholarly output, ground-breaking publications, achievement of excellence grants, and international research network.
Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

To qualify for the position, you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

 

Application requirements
The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborate research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
Up to five of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload a pdf for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

• 
Teaching Portfolio as documentation for teaching and learning experience as well as supervision qualifications. Any format is acceptable, but you can find inspiration for structuring your teaching portfolio on the Faculty's teaching portfolio page.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

Submission guidelines

• 
All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be protected by password. 

• 
Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. 

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation and references may be obtained. 

 

About SDU
SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.
SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

How to apply
Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply online" link provided in the job posting.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.
 

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in material flow analysis and resource management
jobs.description:
The SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology, University of Southern Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in material flow analysis and resource management. The position is initially offered for one year, with the possibility of extension depending on available funding.

The position will focus on quantitative assessment of material and resource systems. The work will involve analysis of material stocks and flows, resource use, waste management and recycling, and associated environmental impacts across different material systems and end-use sectors.

The postdoc will apply material flow analysis, life cycle assessment and scenario analysis to support research on resource and waste management. Application areas may include plastics, phosphorus, critical raw materials and other material systems.

The position will contribute to ongoing research projects and activities at SDU Life Cycle Engineering.

Main tasks

The main tasks include:

·         Quantifying material stocks and flows across different material systems and end-use sectors

·         Assessing secondary resource availability and future resource demand

·         Applying life cycle assessment and scenario analysis

·         Contributing to scientific publications and research projects

·         Contributing to teaching and supervision within relevant areas

Qualifications

The successful candidate should have:

·         A PhD in environmental engineering, industrial ecology, environmental science or a related field

·         Strong experience with material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, and scenario analysis

·         Strong quantitative and analytical skills

·         A strong publication record in relevant international journals

·         Experience in international research collaboration

·         Good written and spoken English

·         Ability to work independently and as part of a research team

Experience with plastics, phosphorus, critical raw materials or related resource systems will be considered an advantage. 

Research environment

As a postdoc, you will conduct independent research, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy and energy system optimization.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU and with external partners, including international conferences and research visits.

Application

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

•

jobs.occupation: DIAS Fellow in Engineering within Organoid Intelligence
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Organoid Intelligence. The candidate is expected to start on January 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. 

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST) 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. 

 

Who are we looking for

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of Organoid Intelligence, capable of combining multiple disciplines, including Neuroscience, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science and Bioimaging. The candidate must develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The ideal candidate should: 

• 
Drive internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition.

• 
Publish in high-level peer-reviewed academic journals.

• 
Engage in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
Play an active role in securing external funding, including both EU and Danish sources.

• 
Commit to excellence in teaching at both undergraduate and graduate levels, including participation in teaching, development of new courses, and supervision of BSc, MSc, and PhD students.

• 
Collaborate with interdisciplinary teams on artificial intelligence, neuroscience, biochemistry and molecular biology, bioimaging, and across various domains, also in the framework of DIAS.

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of data science such as AI and machine learning, neuroscience, physics and applied mathematics. Experience working within bioimaging is an advantage but not a precondition.

• 
Demonstrate an outstanding track record to be qualified at the Assistant Professor level by the hiring time. The candidate may have experience at the Assistant Professor level or must be qualified at the time of being hired. The candidate may also have postdoctoral experience and may already have experience at the assistant professor level.

• 
Demonstrate a strong track record of research and scientific publication.

• 
Have a well-documented teaching record. 

• 
Be fluent in English; the ability to communicate in Danish is an advantage but not a precondition.

• 
Exhibit a commitment to excellence and multidisciplinary collaboration.

 

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally. 

 

MMMI

The Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller Institute is an internationally recognized institute, which has maintained a leading position in robotics for more than three decades. The institute is the origin of robotics research in Denmark and has spawned the world-renowned cluster of robotics in Odense with more than 130 robotics companies including Universal Robots and Mobile Industrial Robots. Building on our expertise in AI, robotics and software, we have raised strong research centres in related domains, such as Health Informatics and Energy Informatics, Drones and other relevant research areas.

SDU Applied AI and Data Science (SDU-AID)

SDU Applied AI and Data Science is one of MMMI’s 12 units and conducts interdisciplinary research in artificial intelligence and data science within the medical and energy sector, where we apply artificial intelligence and data science to improve procedures, provide information for decision makers and gain new knowledge.

SDU-AID’s backgrounds span from pure science (including mathematics and physics) to applied disciplines (such as biostatistics, epidemiology, computer science, and engineering). This gives the team a broad perspective on researching new, innovative solutions in a variety of fields.

The focus lies on the application of artificial intelligence and data science to advance research and provide data-driven solutions within the medical and energy sectors. Due to our long presence at SDU, we have established over the years strong collaborations with clinical researchers and companies, both in Denmark and abroad. Together with our collaborators, we are improving the way of handling and gaining insight from data, therefore creating knowledge and value for society. 

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk.

For more questions about the position, please contact Head of Unit, Professor Nadimi at esi@mmmi.sdu.dk.

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The candidate will be attached to SDU Applied AI and Data Science Unit in Odense and is also expected to participate in DIAS activities and interdisciplinary cooperation in Odense regularly.
The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state with the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for tenure track assistant professor as described herein. Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”. 

Further information on salary and taxation.

The tenure track programme the Faculty of Engineering is aimed at the most talented scholars who have established a high level in their current research and other professional work, and those who possess exceptional potential to achieve the highest international level within their research area. Candidates enter the assistant professor level (for up to 6 years) and, upon successful completion, will be promoted to a permanent position of associate professor, subject to a positive assessment by an expert committee. Indicators of relevant scholarly merits include documented independent scholarly output, ground-breaking publications, achievement of excellence grants, and international research network.

Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

To qualify for the position, you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline. 

 

Application requirements
The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborate research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
Up to five of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload a pdf for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

• 
Teaching Portfolio as documentation for teaching and learning experience as well as supervision qualifications. Any format is acceptable, but you can find inspiration for structuring your teaching portfolio on the Faculty's teaching portfolio page.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

 

Submission guidelines

• 
All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be protected by password. 

• 
Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the assessment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU.

Assessment of applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns them. 

Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation and references may be obtained. 

 

About SDU
SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.
SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

 

Equal opportunity employment
The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.

How to apply
Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply online" link provided in the job posting.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11.59 PM/23.59 (CET/CEST)

jobs.occupation: R&D Engineer – Machining
jobs.description:
DAMRC is a research and development centre for advanced manufacturing. We are internationally recognised for our work in metal processing, and our job is to turn new technology into something Danish manufacturers can use on the shop floor.

You will work both in our own R&D centre in Herning, where trials can be run without stopping a production line, and out at the companies themselves, where the solution has to survive daily use.

We are now expanding the engineering team with two R&D Engineers.

Your role

As an R&D Engineer you will work on national and international research and development projects from the first idea through to implementation, at a high international technical level. Specifically, you will:

•     Drive the development and maturation of new machining technologies in our R&D centre

•     Play a central role in process and production optimisation for industrial customers

•     Work closely with cross-functional teams and industry partners

•     Contribute to technologies that support the green transition

•     Share what you find - with engineers, production managers and machine operators alike

Who we are looking for

We are filling two positions and they do not have to be identical profiles.

Essential

•     A degree in mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering or equivalent

•     Real understanding of machining - the process itself, not just the theory around it

•     The ability to explain a technical result clearly to very different audiences, from design engineers to machine operators

•     Fluent English, written and spoken. Danish is not a requirement

Advantageous

•     Specialisation in materials engineering

•     Hands-on experience with material processing and machining techniques

•     Strong analytical skills and experience with trial design, measurement or data analysis

•     Strong IT skills and familiarity with current engineering tools and methods

Ambitious recent graduates are encouraged to apply. If you are early in your career we do not expect the experience - we expect curiosity and a willingness to get your hands dirty.

Eligibility. You must already be entitled to work in Denmark. We are not set up to handle work and residence permit applications, so we can only consider applicants who are citizens of the EU, EEA or Switzerland, or who already hold a valid Danish work permit.

What we offer

•     A high-technology research centre in strong growth, where you are invited to contribute both professionally and personally

•     Direct contact with our members and customers, and time spent inside companies most engineers never see from the inside

•     An innovative, supportive environment alongside highly skilled colleagues who share your interest in engineering

•     Work with technologies that drive the green agenda forward

Living in Herning

Interested in joining an international community in Denmark? Herning has a diverse expat network, and we will welcome you into it.

About DAMRC

DAMRC – Danish Advanced Manufacturing Research Center – is a leader in metal processing and is internationally recognised for ground-breaking innovation.

Our mission is to help Danish companies succeed through innovation and the use of the latest technology. We work in close collaboration with our members, which include several leading companies in metal processing and the machinery industry.

Since 2010 we have completed more than 400 industry projects.

We are a team of around 30 based at Industrivej Syd 17A, 7400 Herning, Denmark.

How to apply

We review applications as they arrive and will close the posting once we have found the right people, so there is no deadline — send yours when you are ready.

Send your application and CV to work@damrc.com with “R&D Engineer” in the subject line.

To hear more before applying, contact Rory Shaw (+45 2253 312/ros@damrc.com) or Sebastián Assain (+45 2222 5594/sea@damrc.com)

Your application and your personal data. We treat every application confidentially and process your personal data in accordance with the GDPR.

jobs.occupation: Senior Sourcing Specialist
jobs.description:
Job titleSenior Sourcing SpecialistJob description:
At BeGreen, we develop and operate renewable energy projects built to last across generations. 

We are looking for a commercially driven Senior Sourcing Specialist with a strong background in renewables to lead sourcing activities and commercial contracting across solar, hybrid, and energy storage projects based in Denmark, with exposure to international suppliers and projects. 

This position is ideal for someone who understands the unique sourcing and commercial challenges of renewable energy, whether in solar, BESS, or hybrid technologies—and who knows that the right supplier relationships and contracts are what make or break a project. Broader experience in energy infrastructure, construction, or adjacent industries is equally welcome, and will add valuable perspective to our team. 

About the role 

You will take ownership of sourcing strategies, supplier engagement, and contract execution across the full renewable energy project lifecycle. Working closely with Project Management, Engineering, Construction, Sustainability, Cyber Security, HSE, and Legal, you will ensure that commercial decisions drive project performance and long-term value. 

Your hands-on knowledge of the renewables market—its key suppliers, technology trends, cost drivers, and contractual complexities—will be a distinct advantage in this role. Whether you're navigating a large EPC tender for a solar park, structuring a BESS supply agreement, or evaluating a new contractor in an emerging market, your sector insight will be central to how you work. 

Beyond large and complex tenders, you will also support pragmatic sourcing for lower-value purchases, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and speed without compromising quality or governance. 

Key responsibilities 

• Lead end-to-end competitive tenders for major renewable energy packages, including planning, evaluation, negotiation, and contract award 
• Develop and execute sourcing strategies specifically tailored to solar parks, hybrid plants, and battery energy storage systems 
• Leverage renewables market knowledge to drive supplier assessments, benchmark pricing, and identify strategic sourcing opportunities 
• Lead commercial negotiations with energy suppliers and contractors, with a strong focus on risk management and contract robustness 
• Manage both complex, high-value sourcing processes and agile lower-value purchasing activities (RFQs, call-offs, POs) 
• Prepare decision-making materials, including total cost of ownership analyses with a clear understanding of energy project cost structures 
• Support early contract management, including supplier onboarding, performance tracking, and risk assessments 
• Contribute market intelligence on renewable energy supply chains to strengthen category strategies and long-term supplier partnerships 
What you bring 

We are looking for someone with a solid commercial background, and we particularly value: 

• Direct sourcing or commercial experience in solar, BESS, hybrid energy, wind or other renewable technologies 
• Familiarity with key renewable energy suppliers, EPC contractors, and technology providers 
• Understanding of the commercial and technical dynamics specific to utility-scale renewable projects 
 Broader energy & infrastructure experience (also highly valued): 

• Experience in conventional energy, oil & gas, transmission, or large-scale infrastructure procurement 
• Background in complex project environments with multi-stakeholder commercial interfaces 
• Exposure to long-term contracts, framework agreements, and supplier performance management 
In addition, you bring: 

• Confidence in leading negotiations and managing commercial interfaces
• A structured, proactive, and ownership-driven approach to work
• Strong stakeholder management and clear communication skills
• Knowledge of EU procurement regulations (Utilities Directive) or the motivation to build it
• Fluency in English; proficiency in Danish or Swedish is a plus
• Relocation packages are not available for this role and a valid Danish work- and residence permit is a precondition
The team you will join 

You will join BeGreen's Procurement team, a group of specialists working across category management, sourcing, and contract management. We collaborate closely, share knowledge openly, and prioritize integrity in both processes and relationships.  

 

What we offer 

• A key role in shaping sourcing practices at a fast-growing renewable energy company 
• Influence across the full project lifecycle—from early development through construction to operations 
• A collaborative, international work environment with passionate and ambitious colleagues 
• A strong focus on professional development and continuous learning 
• Office based in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen.  

About BeGreen 

BeGreen develops, builds, and operates onshore energy facilities – primarily solar, wind, and battery solutions. We are around 60 colleagues from diverse backgrounds. We design our projects to work in practice – technically, commercially, and in interaction with local communities. 

BeGreen is headquartered in Denmark and is part of Equinor, an international energy company. This provides a strong foundation and access to experience and competencies across markets. 

Our values: collaboration, integrity and ambition are applied to our projects, decisions, and the way we work together internally and externally.

37 timers fast stilling

jobs.occupation: Head of Marketing
jobs.description:
About EDL

EDL is a Copenhagen-based design engineering studio. We build design systems, run UX research, and ship production-ready front-end code for B2B SaaS companies across Europe. Our designers work directly in our clients' codebases — no handoff, no translation layer. We are a team of nine, and we are growing.

The role

We are looking for a Head of Marketing to own EDL's brand, visibility, and demand generation end to end. You will be our first and only dedicated marketing hire, reporting directly to the CEO. This is a hands-on leadership role: you set the strategy and you execute it.

You will:

• 
Own EDL's marketing strategy, positioning, and messaging toward B2B SaaS decision-makers (product, design, and engineering leadership)

• 
Drive lead generation and build a repeatable pipeline of qualified inbound opportunities for the studio

• 
Run our PR efforts: press outreach, media relations, and thought-leadership placement in design and tech media

• 
Source and secure speaking engagements at industry conferences and events across Europe, and prepare speakers and material for them

• 
Grow EDL's audience and reach across owned channels (website, LinkedIn, newsletter) with measurable exposure targets

• 
Produce and edit content — case studies, articles, talks — that demonstrates our work in design systems, UX research, and design engineering

• 
Report on marketing performance directly to the Founder and adjust strategy based on what the numbers say

What we are looking for

• 
Several years of experience in B2B marketing, communications, or PR — ideally in or around SaaS, design, or professional services

• 
A track record of generating leads and measurable exposure for a company or brand, not just producing content

• 
Experience with press relations and/or placing speakers at industry events

• 
Excellent written and spoken English; you will write copy that goes out under our name

• 
Comfortable operating alone: strategy, execution, and reporting are all yours in a nine-person company

• 
Understanding of (or strong interest in) design, UX, and how software gets built — you will be marketing technical work to technical buyers

Danish language skills are a plus but not a requirement. We work in English.

What we offer

• 
Total annual compensation of DKK 450,000–520,000 depending on experience, including pension and benefits

• 
A senior, autonomous role with direct influence on the company's direction

• 
An office in Gothersgade, Copenhagen, and a small team of experienced designers and engineers who ship real product

• 
Conference attendance and a real budget to build marketing from the ground up

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on the most effective marketing result you have personally driven — what you did, and what it produced — to fa@edl.dk. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

jobs.occupation: Dishwasher
jobs.description:
About Us

Tandoori Twist is an offering from Tinyhus Cafe, a child-friendly cafe in Copenhagen, Denmark, serving authentic Indian delicacies. 

We serve not only classic favourites like butter chicken and biriyani, but also lesser known Indian regional food, with myriad of spices and flavours as our specilities.

Our cafe Tinyhus serves continental food, also traditional local cuisines for events and catering. 

We strive to provide authentic food and exceptional service to our guests and we look for team members who are self-motivated, proactive and passionate to walk the extra mile to provide exceptional culinery experience for our guests. 

Our people, just like our food, are the ambassadors of our cafe and restaurant. If you like challenges and you are looking for a place where you can contribute positively, overcoming the odds of a new but growing restaurant, then please do get in touch; we will look forward to hear from you.

Job Description

Tandoori Twist, a growing Indian Restaurant and Takeaway located in Copenhagen, looking for a dedicated and reliable dishwasher and cleaning assistant to join our team and help our kitchen running smoothly. If you have similar experience, especially in Asian / Indian restaurant and are proactive & quick-learner, then please feel free to contact us.

Only applications through our career site will be considered https://www.tandooritwist.dk/tandooritwist-career/

Job description

• 
Washing plates, pots, pans, utensils and kitchen equipment.

• 
Keeping the dish washing area clean and organized

• 
Helping maintain cleanliness in the kitchen and surrounding areas

This is a part-time position. The work is mainly in the evening and also during weekends. Please note that you need to have right to work in Denmark as work-permit will not be sponsored for this position.

Requirements

Your profile:

• 
It is mandatory to have prior experience in kitchen and familiarity with Indian cuisine

• 
You are fluent in English.

• 
You are reliable and punctual.

• 
You are proactive and structured in your work.

• 
You have strong attention to detail and cleanliness.

• 
You can work in a fast-paced environment.

• 
You are able to work 2-3 hours daily for 3-4 times a week.

• 
Since this is a part-time position, work-permit will not be sponsored for this position. Unless you have a valid residence and work permit to work in Denmark, your application will not be proceeded with.

We take continuous interviews and the positions are closed as soon as we find the right candidate. Only shortlisted candidates will be communicated for interview.
